Fact.Name: Form 8959 threshold amount (lines 5 and 9)
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 3101(b)(2): "In addition to the tax imposed by paragraph (1) and the preceding subsection, there is hereby imposed on every taxpayer (other than a corporation, estate, or trust) a tax equal to 0.9 percent of wages which are received with respect to employment ... during any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2012, and which are in excess of— (A) in the case of a joint return, $250,000, (B) in the case of a married taxpayer (as defined in section 7703) filing a separate return, 1/2 of the dollar amount determined under subparagraph (A), and (C) in any other case, $200,000." i8959 (2026) p.1, "Threshold Amounts for Additional Medicare Tax": "Note: The threshold amounts below aren't indexed for inflation." MFJ $250,000; MFS $125,000; Single, HOH, QSS $200,000. Reuses the existing formW2s /medicareWagesAdditionalTaxThreshhold switch (spelling as-is), which returns /maxMFJMedicareWages ($250,000), /maxMFSMedicareWages ($125,000) or /maxNonMFSorMFJMedicareWages ($200,000).

Fact.Name: Form 8959 line 1: Medicare wages and tips (W-2 box 5)
Fact.Description: i8959 (2026) p.3, Line 1: "Enter your Medicare wages and tips from box 5 of your Form W-2. If you have more than one Form W-2, enter the total of the amounts from box 5 of all Forms W-2. If you are filing a joint return, also include your spouse's wages and tips." formW2s /formW2totalMedicareWages sums box 5 across every W-2 on the return (both spouses on MFJ; a spouse's W-2 on a non-MFJ return is already blocked by /formW2s/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ).

Fact.Name: Form 8959 line 2: unreported tips from Form 4137, line 6
Fact.Description: i8959 (2026) p.3, Line 2: "Enter unreported tips from line 6 of Form 4137". Form 4137 is not supported: any unreported tips stop the return via unreportedTips /flowKnockoutUnreportedTips (BlockSubmissionOnTrue, in /flowIsKnockedOut). A return that reaches submission therefore has no Form 4137, so this line is $0 by construction, not a silent default.

Fact.Name: Form 8959 line 3: wages from Form 8919, line 6
Fact.Description: i8959 (2026) p.3, Line 3: "Enter wages from line 6 of Form 8919, Uncollected Social Security and Medicare Tax on Wages." Wired to income /wagesFrom8919 (currently hard-coded $0 because Form 8919 is not collected). /flowKnockoutForm8959Unsupported stops the return if it is ever nonzero, until Form 8919 is supported.

Fact.Name: Form 8959 line 6
Fact.Description: f8959 (2026) line 6: "Subtract line 5 from line 4. If zero or less, enter -0-". Line 5 = /form8959Threshold.

Fact.Name: Form 8959 line 7: Additional Medicare Tax on Medicare wages
Fact.Description: f8959 (2026) line 7: "Additional Medicare Tax on Medicare wages. Multiply line 6 by 0.9% (0.009)." i8959 (2026) p.3, Line 7: "Multiply line 6 by 0.9% (0.009). This is your Additional Medicare Tax on your wages." Rate: 26 U.S.C. 3101(b)(2) "0.9 percent".

Fact.Name: Form 8959 line 12: Additional Medicare Tax on Medicare wages and RRTA compensation (to Schedule 2, line 17b)
Fact.Description: f8959 (2026) line 12: "Add lines 7 and 11. Also enter this amount on Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 17b". i8959 (2026) p.4, Line 12: "Enter the amount from line 12 on the following line of your tax return. • Line 17b of Schedule 2 (Form 1040)." Line 11 (RRTA, Part II) is not supported; RRTA returns where it could apply stop via /flowKnockoutForm8959Unsupported, so line 12 = line 7.

Fact.Name: Form 8959 line 13: self-employment income (Schedule SE, Part I, line 6)
Fact.Description: f8959 (2026) line 13: "Self-employment income from Schedule SE (Form 1040), Part I, line 6. If you had a loss, enter -0-". i8959 (2026) p.4, Line 13: "Enter your self-employment income from Schedule SE (Form 1040), Part I, line 6." i8959 (2026) p.1: "A self-employment loss shouldn't be considered for purposes of this tax." Schedule SE line 6 here is scheduleSE /seNetEarningsFromSelfEmployment (net profit floored at 0, times 92.35%), counted only when /seTaxApplies (net earnings of $400 or more, 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)); otherwise there is no self-employment income. Only the primary filer can own a Schedule C business here (scheduleC /flowKnockoutScheduleCSpouseBusiness), so this is the whole return's SE income.

Fact.Name: Form 8959 line 16
Fact.Description: f8959 (2026) lines 14-16: line 14 = threshold; line 15 "Enter the amount from line 4"; line 16 "Subtract line 15 from line 14. If zero or less, enter -0-". 26 U.S.C. 1401(b)(2)(B): the SE threshold "shall be reduced (but not below zero) by the amount of wages taken into account in determining the tax imposed under section 3121(b)(2) with respect to the taxpayer."

Fact.Name: Form 8959 line 17
Fact.Description: f8959 (2026) line 17: "Subtract line 16 from line 13. If zero or less, enter -0-".

Fact.Name: Form 8959 line 18: Additional Medicare Tax on self-employment income (to Schedule 2, line 11)
Fact.Description: f8959 (2026) line 18: "Additional Medicare Tax on self-employment income. Multiply line 17 by 0.9% (0.009). Enter here and on Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 11". i8959 (2026) p.4, Line 18: "Multiply line 17 by 0.9% (0.009). ... Enter the result on this line and on Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 11". 26 U.S.C. 1401(b)(2)(A): "a tax equal to 0.9 percent of the self-employment income for such taxable year which is in excess of" $250,000 (joint), 1/2 of that (MFS), or $200,000 (any other case).

Fact.Name: Form 8959 line 19: Medicare tax withheld (W-2 box 6)
Fact.Description: i8959 (2026) p.4, Line 19: "Enter the amount of Medicare tax withheld, if any, reported on Form W-2, box 6. If you have more than one Form W-2, add the amounts in box 6 of all your Forms W-2 ... If you are filing a joint return, include your spouse's Medicare tax withheld." The same line also includes W-2 box 12 codes B and N; any W-2 with those codes is already stopped by formW2s /knockoutForBox12Value.

Fact.Name: Form 8959 line 21: regular Medicare tax withholding
Fact.Description: f8959 (2026) line 20: "Enter the amount from line 1"; line 21: "Multiply line 20 by 1.45% (0.0145). This is your regular Medicare tax withholding on Medicare wages". Rate: 26 U.S.C. 3101(b)(1) (1.45 percent).

Fact.Name: Form 8959 line 22: Additional Medicare Tax withholding on Medicare wages
Fact.Description: f8959 (2026) line 22: "Subtract line 21 from line 19. If zero or less, enter -0-. This is your Additional Medicare Tax withholding on Medicare wages".

Fact.Name: Form 8959 line 24: total Additional Medicare Tax withholding (to Form 1040 line 25c)
Fact.Description: f8959 (2026) line 24: "Total Additional Medicare Tax withholding. Add lines 22 and 23. Also include this amount with federal income tax withholding on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 25c". i8959 (2026) p.4, Line 24: "If you file Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, include this amount on line 25c combined with your federal income tax withholding." Line 23 (RRTA, from W-2 box 14a) is not supported; see /flowKnockoutForm8959Unsupported.

Fact.Name: Form 8959 is required
Fact.Description: i8959 (2026) p.1, Purpose of Form: "Use Form 8959 to figure the amount of Additional Medicare Tax you owe and the amount of Additional Medicare Tax withheld by your employer"; "Attach Form 8959 to your return." Required here when line 12, line 18 or line 24 is more than zero (tax owed, or a withholding credit claimed on line 25c).

Fact.Name: Knockout: Form 8959 lines Direct File doesn't compute (RRTA Part III / line 23, Form 8919)
Fact.Description: No silent zeros on Form 8959. (1) RRTA: f8959 (2026) Part II line 8 "RRTA compensation and tips from Form(s) W-2, box 14a" and line 23 "Additional Medicare Tax withholding on RRTA compensation from Form W-2, box 14a". i8959 (2026) p.1: "RRTA compensation should be separately compared to the threshold." RRTA compensation amounts are not collected, so stop when a W-2 with RRTA box 14 codes could put the return in Form 8959 territory: that W-2's box 1 wages exceed $125,000 (the lowest threshold, MFS) or the return already has a nonzero line 12, line 18 or line 24. (2) Form 8919: stop if line 3 is ever nonzero (Form 8919 is not supported).
